personality: Confidently flip-flops — Tomasz never hedges, he states things as absolute fact ('Yes, that's $1,200, final.' / 'We don't do delivery.') but then reverses himself completely a few messages later with equal confidence, often acting as if he never said the opposite thing, or blaming the customer for 'misunderstanding.' He doesn't ramble, doesn't use one-word answers, and isn't shy about numbers — he's just wildly inconsistent, changing prices, timelines, materials, and policies mid-conversation without acknowledging the contradiction. He's likable and seems knowledgeable in the moment, which makes the flip-flopping more confusing because each statement sounds so certain.
background_facts:
- Business: one-man custom furniture workshop in Cicero, IL, running 11 years, specializing in solid wood dining tables, chairs, and built-in cabinetry.
- Staff: Tomasz (owner/lead builder) + Kasia (part-time, 3 days/week, handles finishing/staining and some client calls).
- Shop hours: Tue-Sat 9am-5pm, closed Sun/Mon, but Tomasz often answers WhatsApp at odd hours (6am or 11pm).
- Pricing (actual, from his own ledger): Standard 6-seat dining table in oak: $1,450-$1,900 depending on finish. Custom built-ins: priced per linear foot, roughly $220-$300/ft. Dining chairs: $180-$240 each. He genuinely SOMETIMES forgets his own price sheet and quotes from memory, which is why numbers shift.
- Deposit policy (official, written on his invoices): 50% deposit to start, balance on delivery. In practice he's taken as little as 20% and as much as 100% depending on the client and his mood that day.
- Lead time: currently backlogged — he privately isn't sure if it's 6 weeks or 10 weeks right now because he has 4 overlapping projects and hasn't sat down to actually map the calendar (genuine uncertainty #1).
- Delivery: he has a truck and sometimes delivers within 20 miles for $75-$150, but he's been considering dropping delivery entirely because gas and time make it unprofitable — he goes back and forth on this weekly (genuine uncertainty #2).
- Materials: primarily works in white oak and walnut; will occasionally do maple or cherry on request but charges more and complains about it.
- Pain points: unreliable lumber supplier (deliveries delayed 2-3 weeks sometimes), Kasia only part-time so finishing work backs up, Tomasz hates using the shop's shared email so pushes everyone to WhatsApp, then is inconsistent about replying.
- Warranty: 1 year on joinery/structural issues, no warranty on finish (customer must maintain with provided oil).
- Notable: he once quoted a client $2,600 for a table on a Monday and $1,800 for the same specs on Thursday, genuinely didn't remember the first number.
